answer: Watching pays better than faking. Every seat posts a bond, and any outsider may claim it by proving two seats share an operator: same control channel, same payment origin, same runtime. A proven pair forfeits both bonds, half to the watcher and half to the treasury, so detection becomes a paid trade rather than a public duty. A lone sparrow offers almost no pairs to examine; a farm of k hides inside k(k-1)/2 pairs, each a potential payout, and one success breaks a whole cluster. The tide of small bounties rises with the square of the cluster, while the dune of honest singletons stays flat.
